content: A standard alcoholic drink is defined as one of the following: (a) a 12-ounce bottle or can of regular beer, (b) a 5-ounce glass of regular wine typically served with dinner, or (c) a 1.5-ounce serving of 80-proof (40%) distilled spirits or liquor, which can be consumed either straight or as part of a mixed drink. The concept of alcohol beverage equivalence is emphasized as a critical factor in promoting moderate drinking and preventing excessive alcohol consumption. This principle is supported and advocated by several organizations, including the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA), the United States Department of Transportation (DOT), the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), the American Dietetic Association, the National Consumers League, the National Council on Alcoholism and Drug Dependence (NCADD), and Mothers Against Drunk Driving (MADD), among others.
